answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing assumptions, with standing: (1) block names contain ':' only as the 'skill:' and 'harbor_master:clearance' prefixes and ':'->'__' collides with no real block name - to be census-proved in the build by scanning every block name string; (2) the live Linux corpus holds 'skill:<name>.jsonl' files - stated by the orchestrator, not measured on this box; the build handles it by reading BOTH names and folding the legacy file into the new one at the next write, so it does not rely on the assumption being exact; (3) NTFS treats ':' as an alternate-data-stream separator - MEASURED here: an empty file 'skill' appeared in traces/ after the failed write.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder would ask: (a) what is the new name? -> block.replace(':','__') + '.jsonl'; (b) where does the mapping live? -> one public function trace_path(block, root=None) in learning_block.py and nowhere else; (c) what does a write do with a legacy file? -> reads its lines into 'kept' before the TTL sweep, writes the new file, unlinks the legacy one after os.replace; (d) what keys engine_trace_corpus blocks? -> keep path.stem; consumers of the mangled stem checked in the build; (e) how do the probes read? -> read_trace(block, root=traces) which already returns [] when absent; (f) how is the Windows failure proved on Linux? -> the proof asserts the filename contains none of <>:"/\|?* rather than needing NTFS. The ticket carries all of this in decisions.

answers.collision_check: No intention pins the trace filename; learning_block's charter says the trace records every firing and does not name the file. Law 7 (records of truth never collapse errors) is honoured because the legacy file is folded into the new, never dropped. Rule 1: the skill probes and clearance move onto learning_block's public interface (read_trace / trace_path) rather than reaching into it - that is the point of the ticket.
answers.falsifier_check: Clauses: (1) writing a trace for a ':' block name produces a file whose name has no Windows-reserved character, and the write succeeds on NTFS; (2) read_trace over a store holding a legacy colon file plus a new file returns both sets of records, in order; (3) a write folds a legacy colon file into the new one and retires it, losing no record; (4) the three skill probes and clearance count the same passes/refusals as before when fed a legacy-only store; (5) no hand-built '<block>.jsonl' path remains outside learning_block. Horizon: first Windows firing of /idea after the merge.
